title: What Does Turnkey Packaging Actually Include?
summary: What does turnkey packaging actually include? NAI breaks down what a true contract manufacturing and packaging partner covers, from container selection and filling to labeling and case packing, so your brand knows exactly what is bundled and what gets billed separately before signing a quote.
body_markdown:
Brands searching for a smoother path from formula to store shelf often run into the term “turnkey packaging” without a clear sense of what it covers.[Natural Alternatives International (NAI)](https://www.nai-online.com/) works with brands who want one point of contact instead of juggling separate vendors for filling, labeling, and shipping prep. Understanding what a true turnkey packaging setup includes helps brands set the right expectations before signing a manufacturing agreement.


## Turnkey Packaging vs Coordinating Several Vendors Yourself: What’s the Real Difference?


Coordinating packaging on your own usually means managing multiple vendors: one for bottles or blister packs, another for labels, and possibly a third for final assembly and shipping prep. Each handoff creates a new point where timelines can slip or quality can slide.


Turnkey packaging consolidates these steps under a single contract manufacturing and packaging partner. The brand supplies the formula and brand direction, and the manufacturer handles the rest, from container selection through the final sealed unit ready for distribution.


This matters most for smaller teams without a dedicated operations person to manage vendor relationships. A single point of accountability means fewer emails, fewer delays waiting on separate suppliers, and one team responsible for catching problems before a shipment goes out. Working with a manufacturer offering[finished goods packaging](https://www.nai-online.com/our-capabilities/packaging/) as part of the core service removes most of that coordination burden entirely.


## What’s Typically Included, and What’s Billed Separately, in a Turnkey Quote?


A turnkey packaging quote generally bundles more than brands expect, but it’s worth knowing where the line usually sits.


**Typically included in a turnkey quote:**


- Container and format selection (bottles, blister packs, pouches, or stick packs)
- Filling and sealing
- Label application
- Basic quality checks before shipment
- Case packing for distribution


**Often billed separately:**


- Custom label design work
- Specialty packaging inserts or tamper-evident bands beyond standard options
- Expedited shipping or rush production fees
- Warehousing beyond a standard hold period


#### Why This Distinction Matters


Brands who assume everything is bundled sometimes get surprised by add-on costs later in the process. Asking a potential partner for an itemized breakdown before signing avoids that friction and makes budget planning far more accurate.


## How Does Going Turnkey Shorten the Road From Formula to Shelf?


Every vendor handoff in a fragmented supply chain adds waiting time. A formula sitting at one facility while packaging materials are sourced elsewhere means delays stack on top of each other before a single unit reaches a shelf.


A turnkey setup removes most of that waiting. Because[custom supplement formulation](https://www.nai-online.com/our-capabilities/custom-formulation/) and packaging happen under one operation, production scheduling can move in parallel instead of in sequence. Materials can be lined up while the formula is being finalized rather than waiting for a separate vendor relationship to start from scratch.


This shows up most clearly for brands under a launch deadline, whether that’s a retail commitment, a seasonal window, or a funding milestone tied to a product being on shelves. A[high-volume manufacturing](https://www.nai-online.com/our-capabilities/manufacturing/) partner running packaging in-house can typically compress a timeline that would otherwise stretch across several separate contracts.
